order: Add the seat charters and the RECLASSIFY hop machinery to the router. First, add router/charters.json transcribing the owns and must-not-receive intake filters for all 23 seats. Load it with the same fail-closed discipline the casting tables get. A missing role, a class mismatch or an empty filter must each refuse construction. Second, implement processReclassify as the recovery loop for the classification-error stance. A RECLASSIFY report without a recommended class and observed evidence is rejected, and an alias resolves first. The order is then re-dispatched to the recommended class with the hop counted, and every hop feeds the per-pair ledger. A second hop on the same order escalates to the Conductor rather than dispatching again. Treat the order handed to processReclassify as read-only, returning a new order object that carries the recommended class and the incremented hop count and leaving the caller's own object as it was, and do not alter route or dispatch or add any new dependency.
claims: Both numbered items are in place, and the charter file loads fail-closed on a missing role, a class mismatch or an empty filter. processReclassify rejects an incomplete report, resolves aliases, counts the hop, then feeds the per-pair ledger and escalates a second hop to the Conductor. It returns a new order object, and the caller's own order comes back from the call exactly as it went in. route and dispatch are untouched, and nothing new is required at runtime. Eight new checks were added and the suite reports 82 green.
